# Valacyclovir as Initial Treatment for Acute Retinal Necrosis: A Pharmacokinetic Modeling and Simulation Study (Liu T, Jain A, Fung M, Vinnard C, Ivaturi V, Curr Eye Res 2017)

Reference: doi:10.1080/02713683.2016.1231323 (Curr Eye Res 2017;42(7):1035-1038; Table 1 and equations of the Methods).

**Model type: illustrative model only, not a population pharmacokinetic model** (serum parameters fixed to literature values, vitreous partition coefficient estimated by a naive-pooled approach on one paired serum/vitreous sample per patient, Phoenix NLME 1.4; no interindividual variability estimated). Kept for illustration of vitreous exposure in acute retinal necrosis; not intended for MAP Bayesian estimation.

## Notes

- Data: paired serum and vitreous aciclovir concentrations of adult patients with acute retinal necrosis undergoing vitrectomy during oral valaciclovir (Huynh et al. 2008), one vitreous sample per patient. Oral valaciclovir; the article also simulates IV aciclovir 700 mg every 8 h (`adulte/aciclovir_IV/models/ACV_Liu_2017.Rmd`, same disposition and vitreous parameters).
- Serum model (fixed literature values, Table 1): one-compartment, Vcentral 49.6 L, CLstd 19.7 L/h at 30 years with an age effect CL = CLstd - 0.1 x (AGE - 30) (L/h, Methods), ka 0.28 h-1 (Vezina et al. 2010), dose-dependent bioavailability F = 54.5% (1 g), 49.5% (1.5 g), 47.5% (2 g).
- Vitreous compartment (Methods): dAv/dt = Qv x (1 - HC) x (C - Cv/Kp), with Cv = Av/Vvitreal, Vvitreal 0.004 L, Qretinal 0.26 (printed mL/h), hematocrit 47% (men) or 41% (women), Kp 0.255 (estimated, RSE 9.19%). The vitreous compartment does not modify the serum kinetics (no return of drug to the serum in the published equation, the vitreous amount is negligible).
- **Ambiguity:** the Methods state that F was adjusted to the dose size (54.5% for 1 g, 49.5% for 1.5 g, 47.5% for 2 g), but the published steady-state vitreous Cmin (0.932, 1.40 and 1.86 mg/L for 1, 1.5 and 2 g every 8 h) are exactly proportional to the dose (ratios 1.50 and 2.00), i.e. a constant F was used in the simulations. With the dose-dependent F, the simulated ratios would be 1.36 and 1.74. **Choice:** constant F of 54.5% by default (`DDF = 0`); the dose-dependent F of the Methods is available with `DDF = 1` (linear interpolation on the covariate `DOSE`, mg of valaciclovir per administration; 54.5% at 1000 mg or less, 47.5% at 2000 mg or more).
- **Ambiguity:** the unit of the retinal blood flow (0.26, printed mL/h in Table 1) and the dose basis of F are not detailed. **Choice:** 0.26 mL/h (0.00026 L/h) and doses in mg of valaciclovir without molar conversion (F as the fraction of the valaciclovir dose, as in the Valtrex label); these choices give vitreous Cmin closest to the published values. With 0.26 mL/min the vitreous would equilibrate within minutes and the simulated vitreous Cmin would be about 40% lower; with the molar conversion (x 0.694) about 30% lower.
- **Ambiguity:** the age of the simulated patients is not reported. **Choice:** default AGE 50 years: with the constant F, the simulated steady-state vitreous Cmin are 0.93, 1.39 and 1.85 mg/L for 1, 1.5 and 2 g every 8 h (published 0.932, 1.40 and 1.86 mg/L), and the vitreous concentration exceeds 0.82 mg/L after 18 h with 1 g and within 10 h with 1.5 and 2 g (published: 16 h and within the first 12 h). At 30 years the values are 0.83, 1.24 and 1.66 mg/L. The alternative of a molar dose conversion (x 0.694) is not retained: the 1 g regimen would never reach 0.82 mg/L, contrary to the article.
- **Ambiguity:** the article states that the vitreous concentrations after IV aciclovir 700 mg every 8 h fell between those of valaciclovir 1.5 and 2 g every 8 h. With the choices above, the IV regimen gives a vitreous Cmin of 1.03 mg/L at 50 years (`adulte/aciclovir_IV/models/ACV_Liu_2017.Rmd`), between those of valaciclovir 1 and 1.5 g. **Choice:** published parameters kept; the oral Cmin values, which are given numerically, are reproduced.
- Residual error (Table 1): proportional, serum 0.203 and vitreous 0.252. **Ambiguity:** SD or variance not stated. **Choice:** SDs (Phoenix default), variances 0.0412 and 0.0635. Serum (cmt 2) and vitreous (cmt 3) are the two observation types, captured as `PAR` and `MET` (names required by mapbayr; MET is not a metabolite here).
- Variability: none estimated (naive pooled). For mapbayr compatibility only, nominal random effects of 30% (omega^2 0.0862, assumed) are placed on CL and Vcentral; they are not published estimates.
- Target used by the authors: vitreous Cmin above the mean IC50 of VZV (0.82 mg/L; maximum 1.41 mg/L).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mrgsolve)
library(mapbayr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r model}
code <- '
[PROB]
Liu et al. 2017 - aciclovir in serum and vitreous after oral valaciclovir in acute retinal necrosis
(serum parameters fixed from the literature, vitreous partition coefficient estimated by naive pooling, Phoenix NLME 1.4).
One-compartment serum model with first-order absorption, age effect on CL, constant or dose-dependent F, vitreous compartment
supplied by the retinal blood flow. No IIV estimated (nominal values for mapbayr only). Proportional errors.

[SET] end = 24, delta = 0.1

[PARAM] @annotated
TVV    : 49.6    : Central volume (L)
TVCL   : 19.7    : Clearance at 30 years (L/h)
TH_AGE : 0.1     : Decrease of CL per year above 30 (L/h per year)
TVKA   : 0.28    : Absorption rate constant (1/h)
QRET   : 0.00026 : Retinal blood flow (L/h; printed 0.26 mL/h) (ambiguous, see Notes)
VVIT   : 0.004   : Vitreous volume (L)
KP     : 0.255   : Vitreous-to-serum partition coefficient
DDF    : 0       : Dose-dependent F (1) or constant F 54.5% (0) (ambiguous, see Notes)
ETA1   : 0       : Nominal random effect CL (not estimated)
ETA2   : 0       : Nominal random effect V (not estimated)

[PARAM] @annotated @covariates
AGE  : 50   : Age (years) (ambiguous, see Notes)
SEX  : 1    : Sex (1 = male, 0 = female), hematocrit 0.47 or 0.41
DOSE : 1000 : Valaciclovir dose per administration (mg), for the dose-dependent F (DDF = 1)

[CMT] @annotated
DEPOT : Depot, valaciclovir dose (mg) [ADM]
CENT  : Central compartment, aciclovir (mg) [OBS]
VIT   : Vitreous humour, aciclovir (mg) [OBS]

[MAIN]
double CL = (TVCL - TH_AGE * (AGE - 30)) * exp(ETA1 + ETA(1));
double V  = TVV * exp(ETA2 + ETA(2));
double KA = TVKA;
double HC = (SEX == 1) ? 0.47 : 0.41;
double F = 0.545;
if (DDF == 1 && DOSE > 1000) F = 0.545 - (DOSE - 1000) / 500 * 0.05;
if (DDF == 1 && DOSE > 1500) F = 0.495 - (DOSE - 1500) / 500 * 0.02;
if (DDF == 1 && DOSE >= 2000) F = 0.475;
F_DEPOT = F;

[ODE]
double CS = CENT / V;
dxdt_DEPOT = -KA * DEPOT;
dxdt_CENT  =  KA * DEPOT - CL * CS;
dxdt_VIT   =  QRET * (1 - HC) * (CS - VIT / VVIT / KP);

[OMEGA] @annotated
ECL : 0.0862 : Nominal random effect CL (variance, CV 30%, assumed, not published)
EV  : 0.0862 : Nominal random effect V (variance, CV 30%, assumed, not published)

[SIGMA] @annotated
PROP_S : 0.0412 : Proportional error, serum (variance, SD 0.203) (ambiguous, see Notes)
ADD_S  : 0      : Additive error, serum, not estimated
PROP_V : 0.0635 : Proportional error, vitreous (variance, SD 0.252) (ambiguous, see Notes)
ADD_V  : 0      : Additive error, vitreous, not estimated

[TABLE]
double PAR = CENT / V;
double MET = VIT / VVIT;
double DV = PAR * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2);
if (self.cmt == 3) DV = MET * (1 + EPS(3)) + EPS(4);

[CAPTURE] @annotated
DV  : Aciclovir concentration, serum or vitreous according to cmt (mg/L)
PAR : Aciclovir serum concentration (mg/L)
MET : Aciclovir vitreous concentration (mg/L)
CL  : Individual clearance (L/h)
F   : Bioavailability for the dose given
'
mod <- mcode("VACV_Liu_2017", code)
```

```{r simulation}
# Valaciclovir 1, 1.5 and 2 g every 8 h, typical man aged 30 and 50 years, steady state (day 7)
data <- expand.grid(DOSE = c(1000, 1500, 2000), AGE = c(30, 50)) %>%
  mutate(ID = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 1, cmt = 1, amt = DOSE, ii = 8, addl = 20)

out <- mod %>%
  zero_re() %>%
  data_set(data) %>%
  mrgsim(end = 168, delta = 0.05, carry_out = "DOSE,AGE") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(time >= 160)

# Article (Fig. 3, mean simulations): vitreous Cmin at steady state 0.932, 1.40 and 1.86 mg/L for 1, 1.5 and 2 g every 8 h
out %>% group_by(DOSE, AGE) %>%
  summarise(F = F[1], Serum_Cmax = max(PAR), Serum_Cmin = min(PAR), Vitreous_Cmin = min(MET), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(out %>% filter(AGE == 50), aes(time - 160, MET, colour = factor(DOSE))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.82, 1.41), linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Vitreous aciclovir concentration (mg/L)", colour = "Valaciclovir (mg) q8h",
       title = "Liu et al. 2017 - vitreous concentrations at steady state (50 years)")
```
